messages:
maya: Heads-up — saw a billing mismatch from streaming + retries this morning. Client retried a mid-stream chunk and billing shows doubled tokens for that session. Has anyone seen this pattern? https://redwood/incident/INC-762 :thinking:

liam: Yep, saw something like this in canary last month. Root cause usually that ingest treats each streaming chunk as an independent metering event and dedupe only uses request_id, not the (request_id, seq). If a retry produces the same seq it still gets applied.

anita: Hmm. Are we deduping at write time or post-aggregation? Doing it at write time with a strong uniqueness check adds latency in the hot path. Doing it later makes billing eventually consistent. Tradeoff: accuracy vs tail latency. :hourglass_flowing_sand:

liam: Proposal: include a compact sequence header on stream events and make the ingest idempotency key (request_id, seq_number). Example event we could adopt (pseudo):
```
{"request_id": "r_abc123", "seq": 7, "chunk_tokens": 124, "approx_total_tokens": null, "final": false}
```
Then ingestion can no-op when the idempotency key already exists. Final chunk sets `final=true` and includes `approx_total_tokens` so we can shortcut reconciliation.

jordan: That sounds fine. Another option: optimistic KV write with TTL for (request_id, seq) to avoid a synchronous strong check on the critical path. Write returns fast; a background reconciler corrects duplicates if TTL expired. Lower latency but more complexity in reconciler.

maya: The reconciler idea is appealing because for billing we can accept eventual correctness as long as we have an audit trail. Operationally we need: (1) raw event retention (30 days) to support audits/backfills, (2) a reconciler that emits canonical billing events to the ledger, and (3) a failure mode where we mark sessions as "provisional" until reconciliation completes.

liam: Agreed. Sketch of reconciler output (canonical billing event):
```
{"canonical_id": "c_r_abc123", "request_id": "r_abc123", "total_tokens": 3124, "token_breakdown": {"prompt": 124, "completion": 3000}, "reconciled_at": "2026-03-20T04:01:00Z", "audit_status": "reconciled"}
```
The ledger should only charge on canonical events; the ingest pipeline can keep emitting provisional deltas but they must be tagged non-billing.

anita: Concern: adding seq numbers increases event size and could impact throughput for very high QPS customers. We should keep the header compact (single byte seq when possible) and avoid string-heavy keys. Also add a flag to opt-out for older clients (with a compatibility mode).

jordan: For compatibility: accept old events but treat them as unsequenced streams and route them to a special reconciler flow that relies on timestamps and heuristics. Not ideal but avoids breaking older SDKs.

maya: Operational notes: reconciler must be idempotent and able to re-run for backfills. We should store raw events in cold storage and a lightweight index with (request_id, first_seen_ts, last_seen_ts) to accelerate reconstructions.

liam: Implementation detail: reconciler reconstructs sequence by ordering by seq then by ingestion offset. For identical seq collisions (possible if client bug), we apply last-writer-wins with a deterministic tie-breaker (node_id > event_offset). Document this tie-breaker in the audit logs.

eng-bot: deploybot: metering-v2 canary scheduled: prod-canary at 2026-03-21T04:00:00Z. Rollout notes: enable seq header parsing behind feature flag `metering_seq_v2`.

anita: Next steps I volunteer to prototype a compact seq header + reconciler shim. Plan: 1) design header + wire format, 2) implement lightweight KV dedupe prototype, 3) synthetic load + backfill test, 4) canary. I'll own the prototype. :raised_hands:

maya: Thanks! I filed an infra ticket and linked the design doc: https://redwood/issue/INF-3141 — assigned to @anita. Will follow up with a short RFC draft by EOD.

liam: Sounds good. One more thought — we should also add a flag `audit_only` for internal QA traffic so we can validate reconcilers without affecting billing.

maya: Good call. Putting that in the RFC.

anita: I'll post the initial proto PR to the eng-platform repo when ready. ETA 3 days.

eng-bot: reaction: :rocket: to maya, anita
